chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a performer of Tamattu' who clipped his nails and cut the hair of his head with scissors. He said: 'There is no problem, as not everyone can find scissors.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to cut their nails and hair with scissors during Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a Mu'tamir may trim nails and hair during Ihram using a 'mishqas' (a type of small scissors or nail clipper), emphasizing that the prohibition is not absolute but contingent on the availability of proper tools. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of *al-rukhas* (concessions) in Hajj rituals, prioritizing ease (*yusr*) over rigid formalism when practical constraints exist. It underscores the juristic view that the restriction on cutting hair/nails is linked to the specific act of *tahallul* (exit from Ihram) rather than a total ban on grooming.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Safwan Bin yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the performer of Tumatto clipping his nails and taking from the hair of his head with the blade. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem. Not everyone can find the scissors’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) cuts his nails and takes certain amount of the hairs from his head with a blade. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful, everyone cannot not find scissors.’”
